book_rctr_room.description: Find available conference rooms, or prepare a room booking / Teams meeting for confirmation.

attendees.description:
Comma-separated email addresses to invite, e.g.
``"alice@empresa.com, bob@empresa.com"``.

body.description: Optional agenda or description text for the calendar invite.

body_type.description:
``"text"`` (default) — plain text body.
``"html"`` — body contains HTML markup that should render in the
calendar invite (bold, links, lists, etc.). Use this when the body
comes from Jira, a ticket, or any source that provides HTML.

building.description:
Building / room list to search, e.g. ``"RCTR"`` or part of a building
name from a ``building_required`` response. Leave empty to use the
user's office building.

dry_run.description:
When True, return available rooms without booking. Ignores ``room_name``,
``subject``, and ``attendees``.

location.description: Optional physical location string (Teams-link-only meetings only).

room_email.description:
Room email address from ``dry_run`` results. Optional — it must belong
to a room in the directory; pass the same ``building`` used for ``dry_run``.

room_name.description:
Display name of the room to book, as returned by ``dry_run``, e.g.
``"RCTR 2NAA07"``. Leave empty for a Teams-link-only meeting or when
using ``dry_run=True``.

room_prefix.description:
Optional room-name filter, e.g. ``"RCTR 2N"`` for one wing. Without
``building`` it searches all rooms whose name starts with this text.

show_as.description:
How to show the time on your calendar.
``"busy"`` (default), ``"free"``, ``"tentative"``,
``"oof"`` (Out of Office), ``"workingElsewhere"``, ``"unknown"``.
Use ``"oof"`` when the user says "out of office", "OOO", or
"mark me as out of office".

start_time.description:
Start time in HH:MM 24-hour format, interpreted in the signed-in
user's own mailbox time zone (same as ``check_availability`` and
``get_meetings``) — la empresa locations now span multiple time zones,
so this is no longer hardcoded to Eastern.

subject.description: Event title, e.g. ``"Sprint Review"``. Required when booking or creating.

with_teams_link.description:
Attach a Teams online-meeting link when booking a room, so attendees
can join remotely. Creates one event with both room and Teams link.

cancel_meeting.description: Cancel a calendar event and notify all attendees.

event_id.description: The Graph event ID returned in the ``id`` field of ``get_meetings``.

check_availability.description: Check whether one or more people are free at a given time slot.

duration_minutes.description: Duration of the slot to check in minutes. Default 30.

emails.description:
Comma-separated email addresses to check, e.g.
``"alice@empresa.com, bob@empresa.com"``.
Use ``find_person`` or ``my_recent_contacts`` first to resolve
a name to an email address.

start_time.description:
Start time in HH:MM 24-hour format, interpreted in the signed-in
user's own mailbox time zone (see ``my_profile``/``get_meetings``
for what that time zone is), e.g. ``"14:00"``.

collect_meeting_transcript_evidence.description: Collect bounded, structured person-related transcript evidence.

confirm_booking.description: Book the room / create the meeting previewed by ``book_rctr_room``.

booking_token.description: The opaque token returned by ``book_rctr_room``. Pass unchanged.

create_draft_email.description: Save an email as a draft in the Drafts folder without sending it.

cc_name.description: Optional person name to resolve and add to CC.

reply_all.description:
When True (default), reply includes all original To/CC recipients.
When False, reply goes only to the sender of the original message.

reply_to_message_id.description: When provided, creates a reply draft linked to this message ID.

send_to_self.description:
Set True only to send an email to yourself. Requires a new email
addressed solely to you (no CC/BCC, no reply); returns a
``draft_token`` for ``send_email_to_self``.

to.description: Comma-separated recipient email addresses (optional if to_name given).

to_name.description: Person name to resolve to an email address (preferred over ``to``).

draft_message.description: Compose a draft and show it to the user for review before sending.

attachment_refs.description:
Comma-separated references to existing OneDrive/SharePoint files to
attach (nothing is uploaded). Each entry is a sharing/browser URL
(what a user copies from OneDrive) or a raw driveItem ID. Ask the
user to paste the file's share link if you don't have an ID.

content_type.description:
``"text"`` (default) — plain text, newlines and special characters are handled automatically. ``"html"`` — *message* contains HTML markup (````, ````, ``

``, etc.) that should render in Teams. Use this when the message body already contains HTML tags (e.g. copied from Jira or another tool). The HTML is sent as-is — do not double-escape.

find_meetings.description: Find transcript candidates in your calendar, not ordinary scheduling.

subject.description: Meeting name or topic to match. When the user names a meeting, pass it here instead of scanning unrelated calendar meetings.

find_person.description: Resolve a person's name (or partial email) to their full identity.

get_emails.description: Return emails from any Outlook folder, newest first.

email_date.description: Start date YYYY-MM-DD in your mailbox time zone. Defaults to today.

folder.description:
Folder to read. Accepts well-known names (``"inbox"`` default,
``"sentitems"``, ``"deleteditems"``, ``"drafts"``, ``"junkemail"``)
or a folder_id from ``list_mail_folders``.
Leave empty to read the inbox.

max_results.description: Maximum number of messages to return (default 50).

query.description: Keyword search across subject and body.

unread_only.description: When True, return only unread messages.

until_date.description: End date YYYY-MM-DD in your mailbox time zone (inclusive). Use with ``email_date`` for a range.

get_file_content.description: Get a file's full content. Text/PDF/Word/Excel/PowerPoint under ~15MB are inlined (capped at 200k chars, truncated: true if cut); everything else (images, legacy formats, oversized, unparseable) returns a download_url instead. A folder (or other item with no downloadable content) returns status="no_content", distinct from status="not_found" (no item matched the id/path at all).

file_id.description: Graph item ID. Takes precedence over file_path.

file_path.description: Path relative to OneDrive root. Used only if file_id is empty.

get_file_info.description: Get file metadata: size, sharing, modified-by, creator, versions.

file_id.description: Graph item ID. Takes precedence over file_path.

file_path.description: Path relative to OneDrive root. Used only if file_id is empty.

get_meeting_attendance.description: Return attendance for the selected find_meetings candidate.

get_meetings.description: List calendar events for today, this week, next week, or any specific date.

check_rooms.description:
When True, splits results into ``has_room`` and ``needs_room`` buckets
showing which meetings have an RCTR room booked and which still need one.
All-day events, free blocks, and tentative meetings are excluded.
Default False.

period.description:
One of:
- "" or "today"  — today's events (default)
- "week"         — current week (Monday–Sunday)
- "next week"    — next week (Monday–Sunday)
- "YYYY-MM-DD"   — events for that specific date, e.g. "2026-05-20"

list_chats.description: List, search, or find chats — including group chats and meeting chats.

list_files.description: List files in root or folder, with optional search.

folder_path.description: Folder path relative to OneDrive root, e.g. "Reports" or "Reports/2026". Two known causes of a 404 even when the folder visibly exists in the browser: (1) for OneDrive for Business, the drive root…

folder_id.description: Graph item ID of the folder. Takes precedence over folder_path.

query.description: When given, searches the drive instead of listing a folder.

list_mail_folders.description: List the user's Outlook mail folders including subfolders.

list_meeting_transcripts.description: List transcript artifacts for one find_meetings (or resolve_meeting_link) candidate.

list_recent_files.description: List the signed-in user's own recently modified OneDrive files. Requires Files.Read.All. No search term needed.

modified_after.description: Only files modified on/after this date (your mailbox time zone if no offset).

modified_before.description: Only files modified on/before this date (your mailbox time zone if no offset).

include_media.description: False (default): exclude video/audio/.loop. True: include them.

list_shared_files.description: List files shared with the signed-in user from someone else's OneDrive. Requires Files.Read.All.

include_media.description: False (default): exclude video/audio/.loop. True: include them.

list_teams_channels.description: List Teams the signed-in user has joined, with their channels.

team_name.description: Optional filter — only return teams whose name contains this string (case-insensitive). When provided, only matching teams and their channels are returned, keeping the response small. Leave empty to…

include_channels.description: When ``False``, skip the per-team channel requests and return only team names and IDs. Useful for "what teams am I in?" queries where channel details are not needed — avoids N extra API calls.…

mark_email_read.description: Mark an email message as read.

message_id.description: The Graph message id from the ``id`` field of ``get_emails``.

my_profile.description: Return the signed-in user's display name, email address, and time zone.

my_recent_contacts.description: Return people the signed-in user has recently emailed or chatted with.

limit.description:
Maximum number of contacts to return per source (default 20).
The merged result may contain up to ``limit * 3`` entries before
deduplication, typically resolving to 20-40 unique people.

read_active_chats.description: Return all messages from all chats active in a time window.

max_chats.description:
Maximum number of active chats to fetch messages from (default 30).
Chats are ordered by most-recently-active first — the most relevant
ones are always included.

period.description:
How far back to look.  Accepts:
- ``"1d"``   — today
- ``"7d"``   — last 7 days  (default)
- ``"14d"``  — last 14 days
- ``"30d"``  — last 30 days
- ``"YYYY-MM-DD"`` — exact start date

read_channel_messages.description: Read messages from a Teams channel — accepts names OR IDs.

team_id.description: The ID of the team. Use ``list_teams_channels`` to find it.

channel_id.description: The ID of the channel within that team.

period.description: How far back to fetch messages. Any ``Nd`` suffix is accepted (e.g. ``"5d"``, ``"21d"``), as well as ``"YYYY-MM-DD"`` for a specific start date, or ``""`` for the most recent ``count`` messages…

count.description: When ``period`` is empty, return at most this many recent messages (default 50). Ignored when a period or date is supplied.

include_replies.description: When ``True``, fetch and include threaded replies for every top-level message that has any (gated on ``replyCount > 0``, so no wasted calls for messages with no replies). Default ``False`` — only…

unanswered_only.description: When ``True``, return only top-level messages that have received **zero replies** — useful for spotting open issues or questions that nobody has responded to yet. Uses the ``replyCount`` field…

read_chat_messages.description: Read messages from a chat — recent messages or all messages on a specific date.

chat_id.description: The chat ID from list_chats or find_chat.

count.description: Number of recent messages to return when no date is given (default 20, max 50).

date.description:
Date in YYYY-MM-DD format, e.g. "2026-05-12". When provided, returns all
messages from that date and ``count`` is ignored.

read_email.description: Read a single email's full body OR a full conversation thread.

read_transcript.description: Read timestamped, sanitized transcript evidence (not meeting chat).

resolve_meeting_link.description: Resolve one meeting directly from a Teams meeting link the user pasted.

search_files.description: Keyword search across OneDrive (own + shared-with-user). Requires Files.Read.All. query is required — use list_recent_files for a keyword-free listing.

query.description: Required search term (not a bare wildcard).

limit.description: Target items to return. Default 25. May be exceeded (see above).

modified_after.description: Only files modified on/after this date (your mailbox time zone if no offset).

modified_before.description: Only files modified on/before this date (your mailbox time zone if no offset).

include_media.description: False (default): exclude video/audio/.loop. True: include them.

search_messages.description: Search for messages by keyword, sender, or @mentions across chats and channels.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Scopes search to a specific day.

end_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD inclusive. Mentions date range only.

from_person.description:
Person name or email prefix — find messages sent BY this person.
Accepts: ``"smith"``, ``"Smith, John"``, ``"jsmith@empresa.com"``.
Resolved to a full display name before searching.

mentions_only.description: When True, find @mentions instead of keyword search.

query.description:
Keyword or phrase to search for in message bodies.
Required unless ``from_person`` or ``mentions_only`` is given.

search_transcript.description: Literal case-insensitive search inside ONE identified transcript.

search_transcripts.description: Bounded literal search across your OWN calendar meetings' transcripts.

send_drafted_message.description: Send a message that was previously drafted with ``draft_message``.

draft_token.description: The opaque token returned by ``draft_message``.  Pass unchanged.

send_email_to_self.description: Send a draft email addressed to yourself, after user confirmation.

draft_token.description: The opaque token from ``create_draft_email``. Pass it unchanged.

trust_senders.description: Add extra trusted email domains or addresses for this session.

domains.description: Comma-separated domain names to trust, e.g. ``"github.com, atlassian.com"``. The ``@`` is optional.

addresses.description: Comma-separated exact email addresses to trust, e.g. ``"noreply@github.com, alerts@pagerduty.com"``.
